newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks trade in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks trade in narrow range.

text.p: Jordanian stocks were trading in a narrow range on Monday as Middle East peace worries cast a shadow over investor sentiment, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose a slight 0.05 percent to 147.80 points from 147.73 points on Sunday.
A total of 110,591 shares changed hands in 233,272 dinars volume. Of 43 stock traded, eight advanced, 23 declined and 12 were unchanged.
The market has remained in a wait-and-see mood since the recent flare-up in violence in Palestinian self-rule areas.
Brokers say investors attention are clearly focused on progress in Israeli-Palestinian peace moves to give new impetus to the market, after a recent rebound lost steam.

"There are a few selling orders with limited transactions, but investors want solid proof that the peace talks are going ahead," said Nasser al-Amad, head of United Financial Investments brokerage firm.
Market leader Arab Bank, which propelled the index upwards in the first half of September, saw a minimal rise of 0.250 dinars to 242.75 dinars in very thin 240 share volume.

After gradual gains end of last month that sent the market back above 150 points last week for the first time in four months, shares began to weaken after recent clashes flared in the Israeli occupied West Bank.
The market was hit this year by the breakdown of Middle East peace talks and the delay in implementing a limited oil-for-food deal with Jordan's biggest trading partner Iraq.
Industrials led the market on Monday with Jordan Phosphate Mines Company dominating activity with a healthy 47,270 dinar turnover compared to dull trade across the board.
The majority-state owned mining enterprise had a 0.05 dinar rise to 3.20 dinars -- the highest gainer in the otherwise bearish market with minimal transactions.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange shed 0.17 percent to 81.20 points, still 14.99 percent down from the same time last year.
A total of 281,604 shares worth 114,767 dinars changed hands in healthy trade in the parallel market. Of 17 shares traded, five advanced, five declined and seven were unchanged.
